top_fixes: ProtonDance (lines 'Shrink down...' / 'Like two magnets'): the faced orange balls are cute but cartoon, not engraved-house; give them the channel's ink outline weight and real limbs, and keep the magnet prop big enough to read, or this scene breaks STYLE.

CalendarPad (line 'Kelvin did the sums'): the mid-action frame reads '8 800 000 years' while the line says twenty million; make the count visibly end on 20 000 000 (and keep it big, not a small pad on empty floor).

SunScales (line 'Physics said the Sun was young'): the scales are small, low-contrast, with a tiny Sun-calendar on one pan; the contradiction (young vs old) is not name-it at a glance. Put a large dawn Sun on one pan and the cliff and tree on the other, so the beam's swing is obvious.

Line 'heavy water' (Sudbury) has no everyday gloss and SNOSphere is a dotted ball; add a plain image (a giant glass ball of water ringed by a thousand lightbulb eyes, with a diver or a ladder for scale). JARGON check.

Several scenes are wide and dim with tiny figures (ChlorineTank, MineShaft, CountWall wall frame): Davis is a few pixels, so the acting and the lamp story are lost. Move to medium shots with Davis large for the lines 'He filled a tank' and 'Only a third'.

Line 'Billions of them pass through your thumbnail': the sparks rain on a pale street and are small red specks; the thumbnail lens works but needs bigger, brighter sparks passing visibly through the man, or the ghost idea is weak.

Rhythm risk: row 'For centuries people watched the Sun' (E-01 engraving, no device) and row 'Davis fished out' (photo plus tally) are the least-eventful rows; give each a real transformation (the traced spot walks across the sheet; the tally chalk marks turn into years on the calendar) so nothing is a picture plus a drifting camera.

Composition: the banner strip ('GHOSTS FROM THE CORE' etc.) collides with top edges and the 'Eddington' and 'Bethe' frames crop the subject at the right; keep the subject inside the safe third and give the banner clear paper.

84-120s (CoalSun/tongs, ~36 s on one dark brown frame): same tongs-and-scuttle composition for ~7 sheet samples; the 90-102 s flame crown holds identical. Break it with a mid-scene transformation (tongs swing, coal heap grows, a clock or candle-count overlay) or shorten.

396-420 s (Apollo chalkboard, 5 samples): same board, same wall props, tiny figure at the edge; only bars and icons change. Cut to the bars physically growing or pull Davis large; add a camera move per line.
366-380 s (chlorine tank / Homestake): wide, dim, Davis a few pixels, tank reads as grey pipe; use a medium shot with Davis large and the lamp visible. Name-it test fails for the black panel.
60-66 s (cutaway Sun): concentric orange rings with dots read as a target, not a star interior; give recognisable layers (spots, flares, glowing core) or a cut-open orange look.

262-270 s (EquationVault / door) and 222-240 s (E=mc2 on brown): long text-on-dark stretches with little acting; add a visible mass-to-light conversion (a bead shrinking into a flash) so it is a picture, not a caption.

Acting 330-345 s and 426-440 s: human figures (the man at typewriter, shopper, miner) are small, stiff and in dim light; one clear face reaction per beat (surprise at the missing neutrinos) would lift acting above 7.
The ghost/neutrino ending 440-486 s: door scene (ThreeDoors) is small and low-contrast; enlarge the neutrino-in-coat character so the 'changes its coat' idea is instantly nameable.
516-527 s final room: near-empty sill for the last seconds while the tags tick; let the Sun rise with a last transformation (tea steam to sunrise ray, candle lit by the Sun) rather than holding.

owner.note: hình ảnh, hiệu ứng, visual, độ wow không như kỳ vọng; drifting-continents vẫn tốt nhất — cái chính là visual, vẽ, các cảnh ấn tượng, sự chuyển biến, biến đổi
